title: Prove derive floods a large decision store, red-first
action: Add a red-first test beside the existing plan-conflicts tests in packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/state_group/tests.rs. Build a synthetic store of at least 200 active decisions whose text uses ordinary bee vocabulary (route, class, state, name, write, tests, planning, release ...), plus a feature whose cells produce a term set of roughly 30 such terms. Assert that derive_candidates returns a PROPORTIONATE list — pick the assertion so it FAILS on today's code (which returns hundreds) and passes once pcs-2 lands. Also assert the small-store case is untouched: with a two-decision fixture, derive returns exactly what it returns today. Read the existing fixtures (write_matching_cell, write_decisions_fixture, write_rule_home_fixture, around tests.rs:2521-2625) and reuse their shape rather than inventing a new one.
acceptance: The new test exists and FAILS on the unmodified tree, with a message naming the candidate count it saw. The pre-existing derive tests still pass untouched.

truths: run on the tree BEFORE pcs-2, the new test fails and its message names the candidate count
every pre-existing test in state_group/tests.rs still passes
the synthetic store has at least 200 active decisions, so it exercises D3's floor rather than sitting under it
